function: AirComp model aggregation: node selection or weights, transmit equalization, receive factors and IRS phase shifts minimize aggregation MSE via DC programming; learned part is the FL model (pp. 7-10).
system: Single-antenna cloud server (Table I) with K=20 edge nodes, passive IRS with P=20 elements, OFDM with N=10 sub-channels; no carrier frequency stated (pp. 2, 10).
method: Not learned: aggregation designed with matrix lifting, difference-of-convex programming and SCA. Learned element: fully connected network (784 inputs, 10 outputs) trained by federated learning, non-IID, 100 rounds (pp. 7-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: path-loss exponents 3.6, 2.8, 2.2 with Rician fading (factors 0, 0, 3 dB) following [19]; MNIST for the FL task (pp. 10-11).
test_conditions: One setup: 20 edge nodes in a fixed region, 100 rounds, non-IID MNIST shards, 10,000 test samples; sweeps over SNR, selected nodes, coherence time, node count (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Ideal error-free aggregation, all-node selection with noisy aggregation, IRS-free channel, SDR (semidefinite relaxation) for the IRS design; node-selection framework versus weight-selection framework (p. 11).
metrics: Test accuracy versus training round, selected nodes K0 (Q0), SNR, coherence time and number of edge nodes; accuracy gain of weight over node selection (pp. 11-12).
complexity: Per-iteration cost of the interior-point step O([(P+1)^2+K]^3), total O(I1[(P+1)^2+K]^3) with I1 iterations, for node selection and IRS design; no runtime measured (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 10: "The small-scale fading coefficients are assumed to follow the Rician distribution". Custom simulator with path loss and Rician fading following [19]; no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "The test dataset has 10,000 different samples". Held-out MNIST samples only; Figs. 4-7 (pp. 11-12) sweep K0, SNR, coherence time and node count as separate FL runs, and no trained model is applied to an unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 11: "the following baselines are used for comparison in the simulations": ideal, all-node selection, IRS-free channel and SDR applied to the paper's own problem P8. Earlier designs [18]-[20] are compared only in words in Table I (p. 2).
q4_support: p. 8: "the overall computational cost of solving P3 is O(I1" [(P+1)^2+K]^3, with I1 the number of iterations; this is the cost of the node-selection, transceiver and IRS design.
q5_support: p. 11: "we use the MNIST dataset [32] to simulate the handwritten digit recognition task". MNIST is a learning-task dataset, the channels are simulated, and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Preprint (arXiv 2310.07405v1). Included as federated learning over the air (area 7): the learned element is the MNIST classifier trained across the edge nodes, while the aggregation, node weights and IRS phase shifts come from DC programming and are not learned (pp. 1, 7-8). Links are single-antenna but an IRS is present, so the system check passes. q3 is 0: the simulated baselines are the authors' own schemes and an SDR solver for their own problem P8, and the node-selection framework is the authors' own variant, so no earlier published aggregation design is simulated. q4 counts the cost of the aggregation and IRS design on p. 8, not the model size.
